samples.summary: Slides Remove-link button is scope beyond the issue's plan/acceptance criteria
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-clear-formatting-keeps-links-todo.md) lists five steps and five acceptance criteria, none of which mention new toolbar UI; acceptance only says "`removeLink` is still the way to drop a hyperlink". This diff adds a new `showRemoveLink` flag plus an unlink `ToolbarButton` in the shared `TextFormatGroup`, opts both slides surfaces in (`text-edit-section.tsx`, `mobile-toolbar.tsx`) and adds a new design-doc section. The addition is defensible (slides has no link popover and would otherwise lose its only way to drop an href), but it is unrequested product surface shipped inside a model-level bugfix and could have been split out; it also commits the shared docs/sheets/slides component to a new always-enabled control.

samples.summary: Slides toolbar design doc not updated for the new Remove-link button; the change is documented only in the docs font-controls doc
samples.evidence: `docs/design/slides/slides-toolbar-redesign.md:254` ("B / I / U, Color, Link | Shared `text-format-group.tsx`, rendered with `showStrikethrough={false}` and `showHighlight={false}`") and :260 (mobile sheet, same flag list) are the canonical record of which controls the slides text-edit toolbar renders and with which flags. The new `showRemoveLink` opt-in is described instead under a new "### Removing a link on slides" section in `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:301-321`, so the slides subsystem doc is now stale and the slides UI decision is filed under the docs area — the repo's convention is to fold into the canonical subsystem doc.

samples.summary: The trailing-edge "exitsLink" rule is copy-pasted at two entry points rather than shared
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:3364-3371` and `text-editor.ts:3439-3448` each compute the same composite condition (`isAtLinkTrailingEdge(doc, pos) || !!(prev && 'href' in prev && prev.href === undefined)`) and then apply the same `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }` override. Only the predicate was extracted to `model/caret-style.ts`; the rule built on it is duplicated. This is exactly the drift mode the change's own commentary and `...-lessons.md` cite as how #715 and the two clear-formatting key lists happened — a future change to the rule (e.g. also re-arming when the caret is at a link's leading edge) must be made twice. A single shared helper (e.g. `clearStyleForCaret(doc, position, pending)`) would keep one answer.

samples.summary: Pending-style design doc still states the collapsed clearInlineFormatting path stages CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE verbatim
samples.evidence: `docs/design/docs/docs-pending-inline-style.md:128-129` documents `clearInlineFormatting()`: if collapsed, `pending.set(CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, cursor.position)`, and :273 asserts "collapsed + typing → typed run is plain". Both entry points now stage `{ ...CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE, href: undefined }` at a link trailing edge, which this doc does not mention; only docs-font-controls.md was refreshed.

samples.summary: Format-painter comment still calls `href` a "structural inline kind", contradicting the new CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE doc
samples.evidence: The edited comment at `text-editor.ts:3566-3568` says "`image`, `pageNumber` and `href` ... are structural inline kinds", while `model/types.ts:286-292` in the same diff explicitly says only the first two are structural (`isStructuralInline`) and "a linked run is ordinary text carrying a content attribute". Two places now give different definitions of the same term.
